title: Ship Review: Evidence to Launch
objective: After this lesson you will be able to assemble a full-stack launch bundle (contracts, gold, budgets, guardrails, runbooks, residual risks), present it weakest-first, and operate the shipped product with day-two rituals.
why: Full-stack launches multiply evidence surfaces: API contracts, UI states, auth proofs, budgets, guardrails, runbooks — each with owners and gates. The ship review approves evidence, not enthusiasm: weakest-first presentation, conditional canary approval, and residual risks with owners and dates. Launches approved on proof ship calmly; others ship incidents.

blocks.text: Contracts (OpenAPI + event versions, additive-clean), gold (API + UI + reconnect with per-layer scores), budgets (latency p99 + cost per task with headroom), guardrails (attack gold per layer, PII audits), operations (runbooks practiced, review queue staffed, dashboards live), residuals (named risks with owners + dates). Each section measured or contracted — manifest-audited like every capstone before.

blocks.caption: Manifest-first launch: gates per section, honesty per residual

blocks.text: Present weakest segment first (the 10/10 with a caveat beats hidden 7/12s), then gates, then budgets — approval conditional (canary-gated %) by default, full traffic on measured green. Residual risks open the meeting, not buried in appendix: honesty up front earns the trust that carries the launch.

blocks.title: Audit the bundle
blocks.note: Run it: expect six PASS lines then conditional approval — including the honestly-noted 9/10 UI gold. Weakest-first with named handling passes review; hidden weakness blocks it.

items: Bundle: contracts + gold (API/UI/reconnect) + budgets + guardrails + ops + owned residuals
Weakest-first presentation; conditional canary approval default; full traffic on measured green
Day-two rituals (re-scores, budgets, chaos, gap audits) compound or decay — scheduled either way

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the bundle audit and confirm conditional approval with the noted weakness. (b) Drop UI gold to 7/10 unexplained and state the review outcome. (c) Draft your capstone bundle skeleton (same six sections) with one evidence line per section.
hints: Baseline: 6 PASS + conditional (9/10 UI noted with handling beats hidden 7/12s).
Unexplained 7/10 → BLOCKED until named with fix-or-accept decision (weakness without handling fails review).
Your skeleton needs per-section evidence lines (contracts, gold scores, margins, guard proofs, ops staffing, owned residuals).
exercise.why: Named-weakness approval (honesty passes) vs unexplained weakness (blocks) plus skeleton coverage are the three launch judgments — evidence graded, not enthusiasm.
exercise.code: // Launch-audit pattern: per-section evidence + owned residuals.

quiz.q: Green averages, one unnamed weak segment. Verdict?
options: Block until weakest named with fix-or-accept handling — hidden weakness fails review
quiz.explain: Weakest-first honesty: named weakness with handling passes; concealed weakness blocks. Averages conceal by construction.

options: Conditionally (canary %) with measured promotion after — meetings scope, canaries scale
quiz.explain: Conditional approval default: canary-gated percentages with vetoes armed, promotion on measured green.

options: Rituals: re-scores, budgets, chaos, gap audits on schedule — findings become next cycle's prevention
quiz.explain: Monotonic improvement is ritual-driven; hope-driven systems decay silently. Schedule or slide.

summary: Evidence bundles, weakest-first reviews, conditional approvals, day-two rituals. Launches approved on proof with owned residuals — then operated into improvement.
